_about: Nests & dens (List 21, #203): wild den sites as content on areas (#7). Governing law: #84's roster-binding in structural form — a place may only SOUND of species it stocks (#84); a den may only HOUSE species its area's table stocks. A den of an unstocked species is not rare content but a data error, and the derivation below makes it inexpressible: the den record names no species at all.

den_record.denKind: one of nest | den | burrow | roost — a FORM word; names the structure, never the species
den_record.interiorSeat: null | a #119 interior id — set only by #119 seating the den (see enterability)

discovery: #137's atlas grammar over #12 evidence (unknown / hinted / open) — no separate discovery store. A hinted den is a legitimate source for #89 tracking reads and #160's sign: class.
enterability: A den record is NOT an interior. It becomes enterable only if #119 seats it — an interior record in #119's home citing the den; the seat is #119's act, proposed there, never assumed here. Most dens are read from outside only: sign, sound (#84), #152 behaviour at the den mouth.
forest_wording_exact: The Dark Forest HAS dens. Of the depths, the record says only: THE DEPTHS HAVE NONE THAT ARE RECORDED. That is an absence of record, not a recorded absence — no depths rule a future canon act would need to break, and no depths content asserted. Any stronger sentence, in either direction, misquotes this system. (The epistemic mirror of #163: there, records exist and leak nothing; here, there is nothing to leak.)
no_capture_guarantee: Encounters at a den roll on #7/#38 exactly as anywhere. A den changes what can be READ — sign, stock, behaviour — never what must appear.
occupancy: DERIVED at read time from the area's #7 spawn table: the den shelters what the table stocks, filtered by any shelter class the table itself carries; where the table carries none, occupancy reads as the area's stock generally (a shelter of the place, not of a species). Stored occupancy would rot against table edits; derivation cannot.
open_register: every den instance (world content, authored with its areas)
whether spawn tables carry a shelter class at all (a proposal into #7's home — its owner's call; the general-stock reading is the honest default until then)
which dens, if any, #119 ever seats as interiors
